title: Moiré-induced altermagnetism from nonmagnetic constituents
authors: Jingtian Shi, Maxim Khodas, Ivar Martin
abstract: We propose a mechanism for nonmagnetic materials to develop altermagnetic order by moiré interference with nonmagnetic substrate, which is driven by structural relaxation and spontaneous twirls in moiré domain walls of lattice-mismatched moiré square lattices. When doped with one electron per moiré domain, a correlated insulating gap is opened by electron interaction. Depending on the location of the moiré potential minima, the moiré bands can show d-wave or g-wave altermagnetic splitting. The former can be enhanced by a finite twist angle; the latter is sensitive to strains that drive a transition to d-wave.
summary: This work details how structural distortions in moiré superlattices of nonmagnetic materials can induce altermagnetism. By combining continuum elasticity theory with Hartree-Fock calculations, the authors show that electron interactions, mediated by moiré potential variations, open correlated gaps and generate symmetry-protected spin splittings. This magnetic order is highly tunable by external strains and twist angles.
main_problem: The paper proposes a mechanism for nonmagnetic materials to develop altermagnetic order through moiré interference, driven by structural relaxation and spontaneous twirls in moiré domain walls.
main_result: The moiré potential, coupled with electron interactions, opens a correlated insulating gap and induces spin-splitting that can manifest as $d$-wave or $g$-wave altermagnetism, which is tunable by twist angle and strain.
method: The study uses theoretical modeling involving continuum elasticity for lattice relaxation and self-consistent Hartree-Fock theory to solve for spin-resolved mean-field band structures.
model_or_system: The system is a moiré lattice formed by lattice-mismatched nonmagnetic layers. The physics is modeled using an effective continuum Hamiltonian incorporating kinetic energy, deformation potential, and electron-electron interactions (Hubbard physics).
key_observables: Altermagnetic spin splitting ($\Delta E_k$), spin density map ($ho_s(\mathbf{r})$), and anisotropic transport properties.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta$), strain components ($	ext{B1g}, 	ext{B2g}$), and electron interaction strength (Hubbard coupling).
main_assumptions: Assumes collinear spins and initially neglects SOC for some analyses; the model relies on continuum elasticity approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate lattice relaxation, Wannier orbitals for different domain types, non-interacting band structures, and spin-resolved mean-field band structures showing the evolution of spin splitting with twist angle and strain.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the structural mechanism (lattice relaxation/domain walls) to developing the electronic model (Hamiltonian/HF theory), and finally analyzing the resulting magnetic order (altermagnetism) and its tunability via external parameters like strain and twist.
why_interesting: The focus on emergent magnetism (altermagnetism) in nonmagnetic, structurally tunable systems is highly relevant to understanding correlated phases in novel quantum materials, which often bridge concepts from condensed matter theory and quantum simulation.
